---
title: "check-heading-levels.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only check that flags a heading that breaks its page's outline.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-30) is that a page's title is its level 1 heading,
so the body starts at level 2,
and each heading is at most one level deeper than the one before it.
Pages split out of larger pages kept the headings of the page they came from,
and a shared include opened ten chapters one level too deep.

The check reports three mistakes:

- **Skipped level.**
  A heading more than one level deeper than the heading before it in the same file
  (`##` then `####`).
  The first heading of a page is compared with the title, level 1.
  The first heading of an included subfile is compared with nothing,
  since it takes its level from the page that includes it.
- **Page starts too deep.**
  The first heading a page renders, following its `{{< include >}}` shortcodes,
  is deeper than level 2.
  The finding sits on that heading, in the include that holds it.
- **Title repeated as a heading.**
  The first heading a page renders is a level 2 heading
  that repeats the page's `title:`.

A page is a `.qmd` file with a `title:` in its front matter.
A file without one is an include, whatever its name.

The check does not count:

- a heading inside any fenced div, or in a file included from inside one
  (the `####` title of a definition or exercise div is the lab's convention);
- a heading inside a code fence, an HTML comment or the YAML front matter;
- a heading on a line carrying `<!-- check-heading-levels: allow -->`.

## Scope

A finding is reported only when the heading line that causes it
was added in the pull request.
The whole page and its includes are parsed,
since the first heading may sit in a file the diff did not touch.
A blank added line is not content.
A heading moved to another place is flagged like a new one,
since the break depends on the headings around it.

With no `base-ref`, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree.
Set `whole-tree: true` to scan every tracked page in full on purpose,
which measures how many headings a corpus carries that break the outline.

## Inputs

| Input          | Type    | Default    | Description |
| -------------- | ------- | ---------- | ----------- |
| `globs`        | string  | `'*.qmd'`  | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive by default). |
| `paths-ignore` | string  | `''`       | Comma- or newline-separated glob patterns (relative paths) to skip. Supports `*`, `?` and recursive `**`. |
| `fail`         | boolean | `false`    | Fail the workflow when a heading breaks its page's outline. The default gives warning annotations only. |
| `whole-tree`   | boolean | `false`    | Scan every tracked page in full instead of only a PR's added lines. |
| `python-version` | string | `'3.x'`   | Python version to set up. |
| `runs-on` | string | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label for the job. Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository; never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it ([#1167](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1167)). |

## Permissions

Only `contents: read` (the default), so no `permissions:` block is needed.

## Example

```yaml
# Copy to .github/workflows/check-heading-levels.yml in your repo.
# Diff-scoped check: flags a heading that breaks its page's outline when a PR adds
# the heading line: a skipped level (## then ####), a page whose first heading is
# deeper than level 2, or a first heading that repeats the page title.
# Warn-only by default.
# Only contents:read is needed (the default), so no permissions block is required.
name: Check heading levels

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  check:
    uses: Morrison-Lab/gha/.github/workflows/check-heading-levels.yml@v3
    # with:
    #   globs: '*.qmd'                         # pathspecs to check (recursive)
    #   paths-ignore: 'chapters/outtakes/**'   # skip known-noisy paths
    #   fail: true                             # block instead of warn (defaults to false)
    #   whole-tree: true                       # scan every page, not just a PR's additions
```

See
[`examples/check-heading-levels.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-heading-levels.yml)
for the full caller stub.
